clue.text: Transport from trap, turning a constant worry

indicators.note: turning says the word for a trap is flipped round and read backwards

parts.note: a web is a spider's trap
an itch is a nagging, constant urge or worry

explanation.surface: Someone is moved away from a trap, turning a recurring anxiety over in their mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses WEB to give BEW. 'Transport' is the verb meaning to enchant or carry away emotionally, not a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: To transport someone is to enrapture or entrance them, a synonym for casting a spell over them.

clue.text: Invited, in poor English

parts.note: poor means bad

explanation.surface: Someone was asked along, but in clumsy English.
explanation.definitionFit: Bade is a past tense of bid, which can mean to invite, as in bidding guests welcome.

clue.text: Saw them playing for team

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are in action and moved into a new order

explanation.surface: A fan watched the side in action.
explanation.walkthrough: West Ham United is a London football club.
explanation.definitionFit: West Ham United is a Premier League football club, an example of a sports team.

clue.text: Saying that place is the opposition's

indicators.note: Saying means speaking aloud, so the spoken form counts rather than the spelling

parts.note: there means that place

explanation.surface: Remarking that a ground belongs to the visiting side.
explanation.definitionFit: The possessive pronoun means belonging to them, here the other side.

clue.text: Gull in swirling wind caught by snare

indicators.note: caught by says the jumbled letters are held inside the snare's letters

parts.note: a hook snares a fish

indicators.note: swirling suggests the letters of wind being blown into a new order

explanation.surface: A seabird is blown about in a gale and caught in a trap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gull' looks like the seabird but is the verb, to dupe; 'swirling' scrambles the wind and 'caught by' sets that jumble inside the snare.
explanation.definitionFit: To gull someone is to fool or trick them, a synonym for deceive.

clue.text: Commander grabs girl: typical!

indicators.note: grabs says the commander's letters hold the girl inside them

parts.note: CIC is short for commander-in-chief
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: An exasperated remark that a commanding officer making a pass at a woman is just what you'd expect.
explanation.definitionFit: A classic example is a typical, archetypal one, so the words are synonyms in this exclamatory sense.

clue.text: Price of horse shortened

indicators.note: shortened says the word for horse loses its last letter

parts.note: a charger is a warhorse

explanation.surface: The cost of a horse has been reduced.
explanation.definitionFit: A charge is the fee asked for something, a synonym of price.

clue.text: Sign of activity in first-class brain?

definitions.text: Sign of activity in first-class brain?

parts.words: Sign of activity in first-class brain?
parts.note: an electrical rhythm of the waking brain, its name beginning with the Greek letter that means first-class or top grade

explanation.walkthrough: Alpha means first-class, as in an alpha male, and these brain rhythms show on an EEG.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpha rhythms are electrical oscillations recorded from a relaxed waking brain, so they signal brain activity.

clue.text: After some games, just going to be fine

indicators.note: After places the word for just following the tennis term

parts.note: a set in tennis is a group of games
fair means just

explanation.surface: After a few matches, things look set to be all right.
explanation.definitionFit: A barometer reading of set fair forecasts settled, fine weather ahead.

clue.text: Restrictions damaged one of a group of businesses

definitions.text: one of a group of businesses

parts.note: chains are restraints
tore means damaged, ripped

explanation.surface: Regulations harmed a member of a commercial group.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop belonging to a chain is one outlet of a group under common ownership.

clue.text: Hides demon admirer? Not all suspected wife

indicators.note: Not all says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A puzzling phrase about someone concealing a devilish fan, then a remark that not every wife is under suspicion.
explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's Othello, the title character wrongly suspects his wife of infidelity and kills her.
explanation.definitionFit: Othello's wife in Shakespeare's tragedy is falsely suspected of adultery, so she is the classic suspected spouse.

clue.text: Bread is mine, thank you very much

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine
ta is British informal for thank you

explanation.surface: Someone snatches the bread, claiming it as theirs with a cheeky thanks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mine' looks like the possessive but is the noun, a pit.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitta is a flat Middle Eastern bread that opens into a pocket, so it is one kind of loaf.

clue.text: Another problem: Mary's no-longer-little lamb has to be sold at a profit

parts.note: her stands for Mary's, as in 'Mary had a little lamb'
a lamb that has grown up is a ewe
go means be sold, as at an auction
a gain is a profit

explanation.surface: A nursery-rhyme twist: Mary's lamb has grown up and must be sold off at a profit.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme is 'Mary had a little lamb'; grown up, her lamb becomes HER EWE.
explanation.definitionFit: The weary exclamation greets yet another recurrence of trouble, so it stands in for another problem.

clue.text: A man of principle? I'm scared he is corrupt

indicators.note: is corrupt says these letters are spoiled and set out in another order

explanation.surface: A principled man frets that his own integrity is compromised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A man of principle' sounds moral, but refers to Archimedes' principle of buoyancy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek scientist is known for Archimedes' principle of displacement, so he is literally a man with a principle.

clue.text: Tweeter losing his head and not making much sense

indicators.note: losing his head says the bird's name drops its first letter

parts.note: a brambling is a finch, a bird that tweets

explanation.surface: A Twitter user who has lost the plot is posting nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tweeter' suggests a social-media user, but it is a songbird, the brambling, a finch.
explanation.definitionFit: Rambling talk wanders aimlessly, so it is incoherent and makes little sense.

clue.text: Sort of binder mostly found in autumn?

definitions.meaning: a ring file whose pages can be removed and added
autumn is the season when foliage is detached and falling from trees

explanation.surface: A kind of folder that turns up most often in the fall.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a ring binder's removable pages and, literally, a detached leaf of autumn.

clue.text: I repeat: Queen Catherine on throne at last? On the contrary

parts.note: Catherine Parr was Henry VIII's sixth queen

indicators.note: at last, on the contrary, means the opposite of last letters, so take the first letters of the words

explanation.surface: A question whether Queen Catherine finally took the throne, answered with a contradiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at last? On the contrary' turns 'last' into 'first', giving O and T from 'on throne'.
explanation.definitionFit: A parrot is a bird that mimics speech, saying back whatever it hears, a fitting speaker of the definition.

clue.text: Put up ladies dining-room over a home for heroes

indicators.note: Put up in a down clue means the letters are raised, read from bottom to top

parts.note: a lav, lavatory, is a ladies' room
a hall is a college dining-room

explanation.surface: Instructions to fit out the ladies' room and dining-room in a veterans' home.
explanation.walkthrough: In Norse myth, Valhalla is the hall where slain warriors feast.
explanation.definitionFit: In Norse mythology, the hall of Odin receives the souls of warriors fallen in battle.

clue.text: Hard men saving shocking treatment for bully

indicators.note: saving means holding in reserve, so the outer letters keep the treatment inside

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers
ECT is electroconvulsive therapy, treatment by electric shock

explanation.surface: Tough men spare a victim from cruel treatment by a bully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shocking' looks like an adjective of outrage but is literal: electric shock therapy.
explanation.definitionFit: To hector is to browbeat and intimidate, so the verb is a synonym of bully.

clue.text: Starch silly man put into sparkling wine

indicators.note: put into says the fool goes inside the wine's letters

parts.note: cava is Spanish sparkling wine
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A fool adds starch to a glass of fizz.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassava is a tropical root that is a major source of starch, such as tapioca.

clue.text: Acquire hide, putting away cape

indicators.note: putting away means removing, so the abbreviation is dropped from the phrase

parts.note: take cover means to hide
C is the map abbreviation for cape

explanation.surface: Someone gets hold of an animal skin and puts the cloak aside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hide' looks like an animal skin but is the verb, to take cover.
explanation.definitionFit: To take over a company is to acquire control of it, so the phrasal verb is a synonym.

clue.text: Over time, surgeon getting name as experienced performer

indicators.note: Over in a down clue places the surgeon's letters above the period's

parts.note: a vet is an animal surgeon
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: As the years pass, a surgeon earns a reputation as an old hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A veteran is someone with long experience in a field, such as a seasoned performer.

clue.text: Uniform, originally black, in functional condition

indicators.note: originally means take only the opening letter of the word uniform

parts.note: sable is black in heraldry

explanation.surface: A uniform that was black at first is still fit to wear.
explanation.definitionFit: Something usable can be put to use, so it is in working order.

clue.text: Fighter, one fooling around with school glove

parts.note: a messer is someone who messes around
a mitt is a glove

explanation.surface: A boxer who clowns about with a school glove.
explanation.definitionFit: The Messerschmitt was a German fighter aircraft of the Second World War, an example of a fighter plane.

clue.text: Small picture omits first two in matching clothes

indicators.note: omits first two says the opening pair of letters is dropped

parts.note: a twinset is a matching cardigan and jumper

explanation.surface: A small portrait leaves out the first two people dressed alike.
explanation.walkthrough: A twinset is a matching knitted top and cardigan worn together, a classic British women's outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: An inset is a small image set within a larger picture or map.

clue.text: Turning up, bumped into one couple

indicators.note: Turning up in a down clue means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: met means bumped into
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Arriving, someone ran into one pair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning up' looks like arriving but reverses METI.
explanation.definitionFit: Two people in a relationship are an item, so the word is an informal term for a couple.

clue.text: Bowler's foothold finally level

indicators.note: finally means take only the closing letter of the word foothold

parts.note: to rake soil is to level it

explanation.surface: A cricketer's foothold at the crease is finally made flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowler' suggests cricket, but Sir Francis Drake famously finished his game of bowls before facing the Spanish Armada in 1588.
explanation.definitionFit: Drake is the most famous player of the lawn game of bowls in English legend.

clue.text: The wit to distribute replies having hacked into phone company

indicators.note: having hacked into says the jumbled letters have broken inside the company's letters

parts.note: BT is British Telecom, the UK phone company

indicators.note: to distribute means to spread the letters about into a new order

explanation.surface: A clever joker sends out responses after hacking into a telecoms firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The wit' is a person, not a quality: the French phrase names a cultivated, witty individual. 'to distribute' scrambles the replies and 'having hacked into' puts them within the phone company.
explanation.definitionFit: A bel esprit is a person of refined, lively intelligence, so the French term means a witty person.

clue.text: Pinch a bit

definitions.meaning: to pinch is to steal or swipe something
a bit is the mouthpiece for a horse

explanation.surface: Take a small amount.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to steal and a plain kind of horse's bridle mouthpiece.

clue.text: In Chekhov, perhaps, reversing my 'hot' for 'cold', say

parts.note: Anton was the first name of Chekhov, a Russian playwright, given as an example of someone so named

indicators.note: reversing says the word my is read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone notices that a Chekhov translation has turned their 'hot' into 'cold'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot and cold are opposites, so one is a word of opposite meaning to the other.
